Subject: MAP: performance benchmarking plan + burst vs steady-state concurrency runs

Hi Jordan / Acme team,

Following our QBR, here's a focused mutual action plan (MAP) item to validate Redwood serving economics for your production route before the final close. Goal: agree a benchmark plan, execute burst and steady-state concurrency tests, capture latency/throughput/TTFT and queueing behavior, and iterate rate-limit tuning for an SLA-ready config.

High-level plan (attached ramp_profiles.csv):
- Windows: Wed 2027-06-22, 19:00-22:00 UTC (two 45m experiment blocks)
- Tests: 1) Steady-state sustain (target 450 req/s for 20m) 2) Burst probe (step up to 2200 req/s peak, 10s holds, 5m mixed traffic)
- Metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency (server-side), end-to-end TTFT, tokens/sec, queue depth, 429s, and backend GPU utilization
- Acceptance: P95 latency < 500ms steady; TTFT median < 250ms steady; graceful degradation for burst (max P95 < 1200ms)
- Owners: Redwood runs, Acme provides monitoring endpoints and golden traces; defined MAP tasks in map_action_items.md

Immediate asks:
1) Confirm the test windows above or propose alternatives.
2) Share any additional request/route-level SLAs (percentiles by route).
3) Confirm the preferred ramp profile from the attached CSV or ask us to generate one based on your observed traffic shape.

Attachments: ramp_profiles.csv, initial_map_action_items.md (in Drive link)

Next steps: if we align on windows today, Redwood will run the first steady-state block, capture logs, and follow with the burst probe. We'll produce a concise results packet (TTFT/latency/queueing) and a rune-recommendation for rate-limit/backpressure changes.

Thanks — Markus

Subject: RE: MAP: performance benchmarking plan + burst vs steady-state concurrency runs — initial results

Quick readout from the runs earlier tonight — attached summary (ttft_latency_results.pdf) and the raw sample points in the Drive folder. Highlights: 

- Steady-state (450 req/s sustained for 20m):
  • P50 latency: 95ms
  • P95 latency: 240ms
  • P99 latency: 420ms
  • TTFT median: 120ms
  • Sustained throughput: 450 req/s (consistent)

- Burst probe (peak 1,800 req/s, short holds):
  • Peak throughput observed: 1,780 req/s (network limited)
  • P50 latency: 210ms
  • P95 latency: 980ms
  • P99 latency: 1,650ms (tail amplification from queueing)
  • TTFT median: 420ms; TTFT 95th: 1,300ms
  • 429s observed: 1.8% of requests during peak holds; spikes correlate with queue depth > 1,200

Interpretation & recommended mitigations:
1) Queueing is the primary cause of tail amplification in the burst. Short-term mitigation: token-bucket global cap at 2,000 req/s with per-route soft throttles at 1,000 req/s and a 1,500 req/s backpressure threshold. This reduces queue backlog and tail P99 in further probes.
2) TTFT is acceptable in steady-state but spikes during burst; recommend an additional prefix-KV cache warmup run pre-burst to reduce initial TTFT for cold paths.
3) For long-term, we recommend a staged rollout with canary traffic at 30% of expected peak and an automated fallback to a smaller model if tail P99 > 1.2s.

Next steps per MAP: schedule a follow-up burst run with the rate-limit adjustments and prefix cache warmup. I propose Wed 22 Jun 2027 at 19:00 UTC for the final tuned run.

Attachments: ttft_latency_results.pdf (summary), raw logs in Drive
